newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda to build new car plant outside Britain - paper.
newsitem.headline: Honda to build new car plant outside Britain - paper.

text.p: Leading Japanese carmaker Honda Motor Co Ltd plans to build a second plant in Europe outside of Britain to produce small passenger cars, a Japanese newspaper reported on Wednesday.
Asked about the report, a Honda spokesman told Reuters that "we don't have any plans at present to build a second European plant".

The business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said Honda had decided to build a new European plant outside of Britain partly on expectations that Britain is likely to stay out of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
The paper said the new plant will produce 100,000 to 200,000 small passenger cars a year and said possible sites include locations in France, Germany and Spain.
Honda has already announced that it plans to increase production capacity at its British plant, currently its only plant in Europe, to 150,000 units by 1998 from 100,000 now.
Honda has said it will invest another 300 million pounds to boost car production capacity in Britain, bringing its cumulative investment there to 700 million pounds.
The newspaper also said Toyota Motor Corp has decided to build a new plant in continental Europe.
Toyota president Hiroshi Okuda sparked controversy in February when he said any British decision to stay out of the EMU might prompt it to build another plant elsewhere.
The carmaker currently has a car plant in Britain which produced 117,000 cars in 1996.
Toyota has said it aims to sell 600,000 cars annually in Europe after the turn of the century, compared with a target of 450,000 car sales in Europe in 1997.

Countries from which Toyota is likely to select the site for its new plant include France and eastern European countries such as Poland, the newspaper said. Toyota is expected to decide the site in early 1998, the newspaper said.

Toyota has remained tight-lipped about the possible site for its new European plant. "Toyota is now considering whether it needs new investment in Europe and is collecting information in several European countries," a spokesman said.
If Toyota decides to build the plant in France, it may consider a tie-up with Peugeot SA and Renault SA, the paper said.
